question:
Read the following passage and answer the questions based on the passage:

A single hive of honeybees can visit millions of flowers in a season, a service so routine that it is easy to overlook until yields of crops such as almonds, apples, and mustard begin to fall in regions where bee populations have thinned. Commercial beekeepers increasingly transport hives across long distances to coincide with flowering seasons, effectively renting pollination services to farmers who would otherwise see poor fruit and seed set despite healthy-looking plants. Researchers attribute the decline in wild and managed bee populations to a combination of factors acting together rather than any single cause: pesticide exposure, particularly certain classes of insecticide shown to impair bee navigation and immune function; the loss of wildflower habitat as farmland is consolidated into large, single-crop fields offering little forage outside the main flowering period; and the spread of parasitic mites that weaken hives and make them more vulnerable to disease. Because bees are also unusually sensitive indicators of broader ecosystem health, their decline is increasingly read as an early warning of stresses that may eventually affect other pollinators and the crops that depend on them. Some farmers have begun planting flowering border strips around fields specifically to support bee populations year-round, a modest but growing practice that beekeepers say measurably improves hive survival compared to farms offering no such forage.

 

According to the passage, why do commercial beekeepers transport hives across long distances?
option_2: To coincide with flowering seasons and rent pollination services to farmers
option_3: To avoid paying taxes on stationary hives
option_4: Because bees cannot survive in one location
solution_text:
The correct answer is 'To coincide with flowering seasons and rent pollination services to farmers'.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage states: “Commercial beekeepers increasingly transport hives across long distances to coincide with flowering seasons, effectively renting pollination services to farmers who would otherwise see poor fruit and seed set despite healthy-looking plants.”

• This directly supports the answer.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Detail and inference questions in Reading Comprehension are answered by locating the exact supporting line in the passage rather than by outside knowledge, even when an option sounds generally true.

 

NOTE

• The other options either reverse the passage's stated relationship, introduce a detail the passage does not mention, or describe a related but distinct idea from what the question actually asks.

question:
Read the following passage and answer the questions based on the passage:

For most of its long history, chess was played across a physical board in silence, its champions remembered through recorded games studied move by move long after the players themselves had left the table. The rise of online platforms has changed this culture more in the past decade than perhaps in the previous century, turning what was once a slow, contemplative pursuit into something closer to a spectator sport, with elite players streaming games live to audiences of thousands who watch not just the moves but the players' reactions and running commentary in real time. Faster time controls, where each player has only minutes rather than hours to complete a game, have proven especially suited to this format, compressing what might once have taken an afternoon into a broadcast segment short enough to hold an online audience's attention. Traditionalists worry that this shift favours quick tactical skill over the deep, patient calculation that longer formats reward, potentially reshaping how younger players train if fast games become the primary way they are introduced to competitive chess. Tournament organisers, however, note that interest generated by faster formats has measurably increased participation in slower, classical events as well, suggesting that the two formats may be complementary rather than in competition for the same audience.

 

According to the passage, what has the rise of online platforms turned chess into?
option_2: Something closer to a spectator sport, with players streaming games live to large audiences
option_3: A game no longer played competitively
option_4: An activity restricted to professional players only
solution_text:
The correct answer is 'Something closer to a spectator sport, with players streaming games live to large audiences'.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage states: “The rise of online platforms has changed this culture more in the past decade than perhaps in the previous century, turning what was once a slow, contemplative pursuit into something closer to a spectator sport, with elite players streaming games live to audiences of thousands”.

• This directly supports the answer.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.
